blocks.text: 6. I/O-Box
The IO-box is an accessory to the BactoSense. It can be used to connect the in- and outputs of the BactoSense to a PLC/SCADA system.
blocks.html: The IO-box is an accessory to the BactoSense. It can be used to connect the in- and outputs of the BactoSense to a PLC/SCADA system.

blocks.text: As an alternative to the I/O-Box, Modbus TCP can be used. Details can be found in Modbus TCP .

blocks.text: 6.1.1 Digital inputs

Use: 4 digital inputs referenced to Common allow the instrument to be controlled by an external voltage (e.g. voltage coming out of a PLC). Specifications: optocoupler input: forward voltage 1.2 VDC with 3 kΩ in serial, cathode connected to COMMON, max. 30 mA, max. 50 mW.
blocks.html:
• Use: 4 digital inputs referenced to Common allow the instrument to be controlled by an external voltage (e.g. voltage coming out of a PLC).
  • Specifications: optocoupler input: forward voltage 1.2 VDC with 3 kΩ in serial, cathode connected to COMMON, max. 30 mA, max. 50 mW.

blocks.text: Additional notes
blocks.html: Additional notes

blocks.text: Digital input requirements The Common (port 18) must be connected to the reference voltage of the input voltage (e.g. 0 V / Ground of the external power source). The digital inputs (ports 14 - 17) voltage range is between 5 - 30 V to produce a logic high level or "1". Otherwise it produces a logic low level or "0". If any of the digital inputs is at a logic high level or "1", the BactoSense enters "PLC- mode".
blocks.html:
INFO: Digital input requirements

  • The Common (port 18) must be connected to the reference voltage of the input voltage (e.g. 0 V / Ground of the external power source).
  • The digital inputs (ports 14 - 17) voltage range is between 5 - 30 V to produce a logic high level or "1". Otherwise it produces a logic low level or "0".
  • If any of the digital inputs is at a logic high level or "1", the BactoSense enters "PLC- mode".

blocks.text: 6.1.2 Digital outputs

Use: 4 digital outputs allow the reporting of 4 different logic states, e.g. errors or alarms. As the output terminals are the output of a MOS-based solid-state relay (LH1540AAB), there is no polarity. Terminals A and B can be used in either direction and can be swapped. Terminals A and B are either in high-impedance (disconnected) or low- impedance (connected) state. Specifications: freely configurable, SSR output: max. 48 VDC, max. 300 mW, ON- resistance 2 Ω.

• Use: 4 digital outputs allow the reporting of 4 different logic states, e.g. errors or alarms. As the output terminals are the output of a MOS-based solid-state relay (LH1540AAB), there is no polarity. Terminals A and B can be used in either direction and can be swapped. Terminals A and B are either in high-impedance (disconnected) or low- impedance (connected) state.
  • Specifications: freely configurable, SSR output: max. 48 VDC, max. 300 mW, ON- resistance 2 Ω.

blocks.text: 6.1.3 Analogue outputs

Use: 2 analogue outputs (4 – 20 mA) allow the reporting of two analogue values, e.g. Total Cell Count and HNAP. Note: For the transmission of precise results, the use of Modbus TCP is recommended. See Modbus TCP Specifications: 2 x 0/4 – 20 mA, recommended 250 Ω load

Check the I/O connections Review the technical specifications in Digital inputs , Digital outputs and Analogue outputs and the schematics in IO-box schematics to ensure correct installation.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. Insert the two M16 plugs of the IO-box on the right-hand side of the instrument. 2. Remove the cover of the enclosure by unscrewing the four screws (circles). 3. Insert cable through the cable gland (A, B or C) and connect the wires to the corresponding terminal according to the IO-box reference table . 4. Tighten the cable gland. Try to pull the cable to see if the cable gland is tight enough. 5. Optional: the IO-box can be mounted on a wall. M4 screws should be used with a minimum length of 20 mm. blocks.text: 6.5 Digital inputs configuration and PLC mode

The instrument can be controlled from an external Programmable Logic Controller (PLC). In order to avoid any conflicts when starting a process, the PLC first locks the instrument into “PLC Mode”, in which the instrument acts as a slave to the PLC. In this mode, all functions of the GUI related to running protocols and other processes are blocked. Once in PLC mode, protocols can be started and aborted from the PLC, using the Instrument’s digital inputs. The digital outputs then provide feedback to the PLC for safe operation.
blocks.html: The instrument can be controlled from an external Programmable Logic Controller (PLC). In order to avoid any conflicts when starting a process, the PLC first locks the instrument into “PLC Mode”, in which the instrument acts as a slave to the PLC. In this mode, all functions of the GUI related to running protocols and other processes are blocked. Once in PLC mode, protocols can be started and aborted from the PLC, using the Instrument’s digital inputs. The digital outputs then provide feedback to the PLC for safe operation.

blocks.text: The PLC mode is a remote-controlled Online mode: the PLC can request a single measurement, or start the scheduler to run protocols at predefined intervals. Measurements started from the PLC also appear in the Online mode results.

blocks.text: 6.6 Digital output configuration
The values of digital outputs are modified in the following situations:
blocks.html: The values of digital outputs are modified in the following situations:

blocks.text: When the instrument is powered off, all outputs are set to 0. When the instrument is powered on, the outputs show the current error state: none / critical / non-critical. At the end of a measurement in Online mode, the outputs are changed to indicate errors and alarms, according to user-defined settings. When Reset is clicked on the output test screen or when Save is pressed on the digital output settings, the outputs are updated to show the error state only (alarms are ignored). After manually clearing the errors, the outputs are automatically reset (and therefore show the new error state and no alarms). At specific times during the measurement, extra signals can be relayed. By default, neither of them is relayed to the outputs. These are: Process running. Active when a protocol is running. Sampling device in use. Active when the sampling device is being used. It drops back to inactive after the sample preparation step of measurement protocols. Low cartridge. Active when the cartridge level is below 15 %, or if the cartridge is estimated to be empty within a month based on the current measurement frequency. Expired cartridge. Active when the cartridge is expired.
blocks.html:
• When the instrument is powered off, all outputs are set to 0.

  • When the instrument is powered on, the outputs show the current error state: none / critical / non-critical.

  • At the end of a measurement in Online mode, the outputs are changed to indicate errors and alarms, according to user-defined settings.

  • When Reset is clicked on the output test screen or when Save is pressed on the digital output settings, the outputs are updated to show the error state only (alarms are ignored).

  • After manually clearing the errors, the outputs are automatically reset (and therefore show the new error state and no alarms).

  • At specific times during the measurement, extra signals can be relayed. By default, neither of them is relayed to the outputs. These are:

    • Process running. Active when a protocol is running.

    • Sampling device in use. Active when the sampling device is being used. It drops back to inactive after the sample preparation step of measurement protocols.

    • Low cartridge. Active when the cartridge level is below 15 %, or if the cartridge is estimated to be empty within a month based on the current measurement frequency.

    • Expired cartridge. Active when the cartridge is expired.

blocks.text: The digital output state at the end of a measurement is defined according to these default values, which can be changed in the settings:
blocks.html: The digital output state at the end of a measurement is defined according to these default values, which can be changed in the settings:

blocks.text: If there are no errors and no alarms, all terminals are set to the user-defined base state. By default, this is 1 everywhere. In case of a critical error, the first output is set to 0. Non-critical errors set the second output to 0. Alarms set the third and fourth output to 0. In case of conflict in the output settings, priority is given to: Critical errors Non-critical errors Cartridge states Alarm
blocks.html:
• If there are no errors and no alarms, all terminals are set to the user-defined base state. By default, this is 1 everywhere.

  • In case of a critical error, the first output is set to 0.

  • Non-critical errors set the second output to 0.

  • Alarms set the third and fourth output to 0.

  • In case of conflict in the output settings, priority is given to:

    1. Critical errors

    2. Non-critical errors

    3. Cartridge states

    4. Alarm

blocks.text: The following procedure describes how to adjust the digital outputs.
blocks.html: The following procedure describes how to adjust the digital outputs.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings. 2. Press the Online mode settings button. 3. Press the Digital outputs button. 4. Set Base state for outputs 1–4 when no errors or alarms are active. 1: The switch is closed. 0: The switch is open. 5. Set the response of each output in the Critical error row. By default, a critical error opens output 1. 1: The switch is closed. 0: The switch is open. /: The switch is not affected by this error. 6. Set the response of each output in the Non-critical error row. By default, a non-critical error opens output 2. 7. Assign each enabled alarm to the required outputs in its alarm row. You can only assign alarms that are enabled. You can assign several alarms to the same output. Example alarm rows: High TCC (top), High HNAP (bottom). 8. Press the Save button.

blocks.text: 6.7 Analogue output configuration
The analogue current output is changed in the following situations:
blocks.html: The analogue current output is changed in the following situations:

blocks.text: When the instrument is powered off, both outputs are set to 0 mA. When the instrument is powered on, both outputs are set to 2 mA. When a measurement in Online mode terminates after cell counting, the value is set between 4 and 20 mA, according to range and source definition of the analogue output settings. If the measurement fails due to an error before cell counting begins, the output remains at its previous value. When a user manually tests the output, the current is set to whatever value the user has chosen. The reset button sets them to 4 mA.
blocks.html:
• When the instrument is powered off, both outputs are set to 0 mA.
  • When the instrument is powered on, both outputs are set to 2 mA.
  • When a measurement in Online mode terminates after cell counting, the value is set between 4 and 20 mA, according to range and source definition of the analogue output settings. If the measurement fails due to an error before cell counting begins, the output remains at its previous value.
  • When a user manually tests the output, the current is set to whatever value the user has chosen. The reset button sets them to 4 mA.
